title: Open dual exchange sends an adjoint section to its restricted adjoint
statement:
Fix the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $A=A_{E,n}$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Work in the finite-Tor constructible categories $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ with the canonical ordinary and exceptional adjunctions and composition comparisons of [def-trf-admissibility]. Let $C,F$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $i:F\to C$ a separated finite-type morphism, and $j:W\hookrightarrow C$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Form the Cartesian square $F_W=F\times_CW$ with $i_W:F_W\to W$ and $j':F_W\hookrightarrow F$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $S\in D^b_{ctf}(F,A)$, $\sigma:A_F\to S$, and let $v:A_C\to Ri_*S$ be its ordinary $Li^*\dashv Ri_*$ adjoint, using $Li^*A_C\simeq A_F$. Let $a:A_W\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj^!A_C$ be constant pullback followed by normalized open purity [prop-functor-package]. For the canonical inverse-conjugate dual exchange $\beta_j:Rj^!Ri_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ri_{W*}Rj'^!$ of [thm-sf-dual-base-change], the ordinary $Li_W^*\dashv Ri_{W*}$ adjoint of
$$\beta_{j,S}\circ Rj^!v\circ a:A_W\longrightarrow Ri_{W*}Rj'^!S$$
is exactly
$$A_{F_W}\simeq Lj'^*A_F\xrightarrow{Lj'^*\sigma}Lj'^*S\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj'^!S.$$
Here open purity is normalized by the extension-by-zero adjunction, and the compact-support exchange $Li^*Rj_!\simeq Rj'_!Li_W^*$ is the map whose inverse has the open-unit normalization of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. No properness of $i,F,W$ is assumed.

source.place: §0.3(a), §1.2.2(a)-(b): ordinary adjunct of the open inverse-conjugate exchange, with the open-unit normalization expanded.

proof.text: Use the normalized open-purity comparisons to write $Rj^!=Lj^*$ and $Rj'^!=Lj'^*$, transporting their adjunction maps as well. This is legitimate for the specified normalization: the open exceptional right adjoint is identified with the restriction right adjoint of extension by zero, not with an arbitrarily isomorphic functor. Set $J=Rj_!$, $R=Lj^*$, $K=Rj'_!$, $T=Lj'^*$, $P=Li^*$, $I=Ri_*$, $Q=Li_W^*$ and $H=Ri_{W*}$. Thus $J\dashv R$, $K\dashv T$, $P\dashv I$, $Q\dashv H$. Write $u:1\to RJ$ and $u':1\to TK$ for the open units, and $b:PJ\xrightarrow{\sim}KQ$ for compact-support exchange. The open-normalization statement, with $g=i$, supplies $\theta:TP\xrightarrow{\sim}QR$ and says that $b_M^{-1}:KQM\to PJM$ is the $K\dashv T$ transpose of $\theta_{JM}^{-1}\circ Q(u_M)$. All these maps are on the finite coefficient domain in the question; the open-normalization theorem is valid even on the ambient derived module categories.

source.place: §0.3(a); open normalization as explicitly supplied in lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization (Stacks 0GL1 refinement).

proof.text: Put $B=A_C$ and $M=A_W$, and in the transported notation regard $a$ as $a:M\to RB$. Let $e:JR\to1$ be the open counit and put $r=e_B\circ J(a):JM\to B$. The triangle identity gives $R(r)\circ u_M=a$: indeed naturality of $u$ rewrites $RJ(a)\circ u_M$ as $u_{RB}\circ a$, and $R(e_B)\circ u_{RB}=1$. Identify $PB=A_F$. Since $v:B\to IS$ is the $P\dashv I$ transpose of $\sigma:PB\to S$, the composite-adjunction hom bijection shows that $q=R(v)\circ a:M\to RIS$ has $PJ\dashv RI$ transpose $f=\sigma\circ P(r):PJM\to S$. Explicitly its $J\dashv R$ transpose is $v\circ r$, and the $P\dashv I$ transpose of this is $\sigma\circ P(r)$ by naturality of the counit.

source.place: §0.3(a); composite-adjunction formula of Stacks Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits.

proof.text:
Apply dual base change to the square with $f=j$, $g=i$, $f'=j'$ and $g'=i_W$. Its inverse-conjugate description identifies the transported $\beta_j:RI\xrightarrow{\sim}HT$ with the adjoint comparison for $b:PJ\xrightarrow{\sim}KQ$ under $PJ\dashv RI$ and $KQ\dashv HT$. Let $\epsilon_1:PJRI\to1$ and $\epsilon_2:KQHT\to1$ be the composite counits. The counit identity for the adjoint comparison is $\epsilon_{2,S}\circ b_{HTS}\circ PJ(\beta_{j,S})=\epsilon_{1,S}$. Naturality of $b^{-1}$ therefore gives $\epsilon_{2,S}\circ KQ(\beta_{j,S})=\epsilon_{1,S}\circ b^{-1}_{RIS}$. Consequently the $KQ\dashv HT$ transpose of $\beta_{j,S}\circ q$ is
$$\epsilon_{2,S}\circ KQ(\beta_{j,S})\circ KQ(q)=\epsilon_{1,S}\circ PJ(q)\circ b_M^{-1}=f\circ b_M^{-1}.$$
Here the middle equality uses naturality of $b^{-1}$ at $q$, and the last is the defining counit formula for the transpose $f$ from Step 2. No ordinary proper base change is being substituted for this specified map.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits; instantiated using thm-sf-dual-base-change.

proof.text:
By the composite-adjunction hom bijection, the $Q\dashv H$ transpose of $\beta_{j,S}\circ q:M\to HTS$ is the $K\dashv T$ transpose of $f\circ b_M^{-1}$, namely
$$T(f)\circ T(b_M^{-1})\circ u'_{QM}.$$
The inverse-exchange normalization in Step 1 says exactly that $T(b_M^{-1})\circ u'_{QM}=\theta_{JM}^{-1}\circ Q(u_M)$. Substituting $f=\sigma\circ P(r)$ and using naturality of $\theta$ at $r:JM\to B$, the displayed map becomes
$$T(\sigma)\circ TP(r)\circ\theta_{JM}^{-1}\circ Q(u_M)=T(\sigma)\circ\theta_B^{-1}\circ Q(R(r)\circ u_M)=T(\sigma)\circ\theta_B^{-1}\circ Q(a).$$
The last equality is the triangle computation in Step 2. This calculation uses the normalization of the inverse of $b$, with its actual open unit, so it determines the morphism itself.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor: open-normalization refinement stated in lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization; transposition uses Stacks 0DV0.

proof.text: The constant-pullback identifications identify $QM$ and $TPB$ with $A_{F_W}$. Under them $\theta_B^{-1}\circ Q(a)$ is the identity of $A_{F_W}$: both the constant pullback map $a$ (after the normalized purity transport) and the pullback-composition comparison send the local coefficient unit $1$ to $1$, and these are morphisms of the rank-one coefficient module. Thus Step 4 is exactly $A_{F_W}\simeq Lj'^*A_F\xrightarrow{Lj'^*\sigma}Lj'^*S$. Restoring the normalized comparison $Lj'^*S\simeq Rj'^!S$ yields the asserted ordinary adjoint of $\beta_{j,S}\circ Rj^!v\circ a$. The argument used the open adjunctions and their normalized exchange, and applies to arbitrary separated finite-type $i$ in the stated categories.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q05-2f40ba36a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item and every cited statement. There are no new nodes and no fixes. Orientation: the thm-sf-dual-base-change square with f=j, g=i, f'=j', g'=i_W gives b=Ex_!:PJ->KQ and beta_j:RI->HT. That beta_j is (Ex_!^{-1})^c, and the conjugate formula of def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate equals the composite in lem-trf-adjoint-mate (1) with alpha=b, so Step 3's identification is literal. Step 2 is elementary and checked: the triangle identity gives R(r)u_M=a, and the transposes are v∘r and then σ∘P(r). Step 3 uses the counit clause ε2∘αG2∘F1β=ε1 plus naturality of b and b^{-1}; I checked every type. Step 4: the only type-correct reading of lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization's inverse-exchange normalization is T(b_M^{-1})u'_{QM}=θ^{-1}_{JM}Q(u_M); naturality of θ at r then gives T(σ)θ_B^{-1}Q(a). Step 5: these are degree-0 constant sheaves and the canonical isomorphisms send 1 to 1, so the map is the identity even when F_W is disconnected. The purity transport in Step 1 is fixed by the statement's own normalization (prop-functor-package clause 6 with r=0, and prop-exc-open-adjoint restricted to D^b_ctf), so it is not an E5 gap. No properness, internal-Hom restriction or stalk conservativity is used. Edge cases checked: j=id, W empty, σ=0. Varshavsky §0.3(a) and §1.2.2(a)-(b) (PDF pp.5-9) give the context, and proof_origin=agent is correct; no SGA source is used. No duplicate: lem-trf-open-square-exchange and lem-trf-open-extension-adjoint state different results, and the parent trace-class-open-restriction uses the conclusion as stated. I accept all five declared tool_uses: prop-functor-package, prop-exc-open-adjoint, lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, thm-sf-dual-base-change and lem-trf-adjoint-mate. They are black-box six-functor or categorical tools that the unit sk-i-curve-zero does not provide, and the prop-functor-package declaration is redundant because sk-thm-sf-package is already on the route. The statement is unchanged and not weakened.
